Separating risks by gene and by age matters, because a young carrier faces different choices than an older one. The estimates give clinics firmer ground for risk management.
openalex-w4407684012:
Soomin Kim and Hiroshi Kori study synchronised states in rings of oscillators. Their paper appeared in the Journal of the Physical Society of Japan in 2026. Many oscillator networks are multistable. The same network can settle into different patterns depending on where it starts.

The authors add two realistic features: uneven natural frequencies and a phase lag in the coupling. They compute numerically how large each state's basin of attraction is. A larger phase lag widens the basins of states with higher wave numbers, up to a point. Slight frequency unevenness instead favours the more synchronised low-numbered states. Knowing which state wins from which start helps engineers control networks from power grids to robots.
openalex-w4416338912:
Shunichiro Kittaka, Yohei Kono, Toshiro Sakakibara, and colleagues measure magnetostriction in the superconductor Sr2RuO4. Their paper appeared in the Journal of the Physical Society of Japan in 2025. The material is a famous puzzle in superconductivity. Its upper critical field seems limited by the Pauli effect.

That effect can create a rare modulated superconducting state, predicted decades ago. Evidence includes a first-order transition and a drop in spin signal. Magnetostriction, the tiny length change in a magnetic field, senses such transitions sharply. The team's high-resolution measurements probe the field-driven state precisely. Pinning down this state would settle long debates about how the material's electron pairs break and rearrange.
openalex-w7163526312:

When DNA-damaging antibiotics attack, bacteria switch on an SOS response that repairs DNA and builds resistance. Olivetol suppressed the SOS response at high concentrations. Combined with it, three DNA-damaging antibiotics needed lower doses to stop bacterial growth, while a fourth did not change. The authors present olivetol as a promising natural helper compound that could restore the strength of certain antibiotics as resistance spreads.

Eduardo Henrique Bianchesi Pires de Arruda leads a team of four physicians in a systematic review of artificial intelligence in internal medicine, published in a Brazilian journal in 2026. Following the PRISMA checklist, the authors searched PubMed, SciELO, and Web of Science for studies from the last ten years. The Child opens volume twelve of Maupassant's Original Short Stories, and it begins with a widower named Lemonnier who loved his wife without a single lapse. He remarries a poor neighbor girl and worships her so blindly that at meals he pours wine into his plate and water into the salt cellar, laughing that love makes him crazy. Twelve tales make up the volume, including A Country Excursion, Rosalie Prudent, A Dead Woman's Secret, The Corsican Bandit, and The Grave. owen-woman-adrift-the-menace-of-suffragi: Harold Owen's Woman Adrift: The Menace of Suffragism is an anti-suffrage polemic dated 1912. perry-present-philosophical-tendencies-1:
Present Philosophical Tendencies, published in 1912, is Perry's critical survey of the warring schools at their height: naturalism, idealism, pragmatism, and realism. Few books map the philosophy of their moment as ably as this one does its own.

Perry expounds each school fairly before judging it from his new realist position. His account of pragmatism, learned from James yet critical of it, is especially valued. The survey's clarity made it a standard reference for students of the period. Reading it now is like reading a dispatch from a battle whose lines still show on the modern map.

Petrie shows signs in Egypt, some in mines of Sinai, that look like first steps to an ABC long ere their age. Each sign, he claims, grew from a drawn thing.

Charts match sign to sign through the ages. His claim sparked rows, yet parts of it have worn well. The tract is the root text of one school on the ABC's birth. It shows Petrie at his most keen.

F. C. Conybeare translated Philostratus's Life of Apollonius of Tyana for the Loeb series in 1912. Volume one gives the Greek text with facing English translation. Apollonius was a wandering sage of the first century.

Philostratus tells how Apollonius healed the sick and faced down emperors. Travels to India, debates with priests, and miraculous escapes fill the narrative. The imperial family commissioned the biography a century after Apollonius died. Readers have long treated it as a pagan answer to the Gospels. History or holy fiction, it shows what a divine man looked like then. Conybeare's edition made the full text handy for English readers.

Volume two of Conybeare's Loeb Apollonius appeared in 1912 alongside the first. It completes Philostratus's Life of Apollonius of Tyana in Greek and English. The sage's surviving letters and a famous controversy fill the back.

The letters show Apollonius advising cities, rulers, and friends in his own voice. Eusebius's treatise against Hierocles then attacks a comparison of Apollonius with Christ. Hierocles, a Roman official, had praised Apollonius above Jesus. Eusebius answers fiercely, giving readers the early Christian backlash in full. The volume thus preserves both a pagan legend and its rebuttal. Few books stage an ancient religious rivalry so directly.

Its subject is the delusions worked by demons, and how judges should treat the women accused of serving them.

Pico writes as a humanist confronting the witch craze in Italy. His speakers debate confessions, flights, and the value of testimony dragged out by fear. He finds demonology wanting in places, a brave stance for his time and place. The Strix shows Italian humanism measuring the witch belief with classical tools. Its doubts echo the Canon Episcopi across a thousand years.

It lets the Secretary of the Interior extend the water services contract between the United States and the East Bench Irrigation District, numbered 14-06-600-3593. The extension runs until the earlier of two dates: four years after the day the contract would have expired without this act, or the day the parties sign a new long-term contract.
plaw-112-140-2012: Public Law 112-140 is the Temporary Surface Transportation Extension Act of 2012, approved on June 29, 2012. It extends federal-aid highway, highway safety, motor carrier safety, and transit programs funded from the Highway Trust Fund while a multiyear law was pending. Fiscal year 2012 amounts are reduced by sums already granted under the year's earlier extension act. A special rule covers the switch. Once MAP-21 takes effect, this act stops, and the amended laws read as they did before it. The MAP-21 changes then apply as if this act had never passed.
plaw-112-141-2012:
MAP-21, the Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act, is Public Law 112-141, approved on July 6, 2012. It authorizes funds for federal-aid highways, highway safety programs, and transit programs, replacing the stopgap extensions Congress had passed again and again.

The act is organized into eight divisions. Division A covers federal-aid highways and highway safety construction programs, Division B covers public transportation, and Division C covers transportation safety and surface transportation policy. The remaining divisions handle finance, research and education, other items, a surface transport extension, and budgetary effects.
plaw-112-142-2012: The Church Plan Investment Clarification Act is Public Law 112-142, approved on July 9, 2012. It amends section 3(a)(2) of the Securities Act of 1933, which treats some church plan securities as exempt. It adds carve-outs for interests in a trust fund tied to a retirement income account. It sits under section 403(b)(9) of the tax code. They apply when the interest is issued to a church, a convention or association of churches, or a related church body. Another insertion excepts a person taking part in a church plan.
plaw-112-143-2012: Public Law 112-143, approved on July 9, 2012, updates a 1960 law to spur building on the Southwest waterfront in the District of Columbia. It replaces the property description with the Southwest Waterfront Project Site description filed with the Recorder of Deeds on October 27, 2009. Transfers to the District's agency may now use one or more quitclaim deeds. It swaps "urban renewal plan" for "master plan", lets the agency lease or sell land to a redevelopment company or other buyer, and starts repealing the old reversion clause.
plaw-112-144-2012:
The Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act is Public Law 112-144, approved on July 9, 2012. It revises and extends the user-fee programs for prescription drugs and medical devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. It also sets up new user-fee programs for generic drugs and biosimilars.

Title I covers fees relating to drugs, with rules on who may assess and use the fees, reporting, sunset dates, and an effective date. Title II covers fees relating to devices on like terms. Its contents add streamlined hiring power to back the review of device applications.
plaw-112-145-2012: The District of Columbia Special Election Reform Act is Public Law 112-145, approved on July 18, 2012. It resets when special elections fill vacancies in District local office, amending the Home Rule Act. For a vacant Council chair or ward seat, the Board of Elections must hold the vote on a Tuesday at least 70 and not more than 174 days after the vacancy. The Board picks the date best for turnout, weighing cultural and religious holidays and how hard the election is to run.
plaw-112-146-2012: The Former Charleston Naval Base Land Exchange Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-146, approved on July 18, 2012. It sets up a land swap between the Department of Homeland Security and the South Carolina State Ports Authority. The federal side holds about 10.499 acres on the former naval base complex in North Charleston, shown as New Parcel B on a 2007 plat. In exchange for three parcels the Ports Authority conveys to the United States, the Secretary may convey the federal land to the Authority by quitclaim deed.
plaw-112-147-2012: The Veteran Skills to Jobs Act is Public Law 112-147, approved on July 23, 2012. It speaks to federal licenses. The head of each federal licensing authority must consider, and may accept, training a person gained in the armed forces when that training is relevant to the license sought. Agencies had to issue any needed rules within 180 days of enactment for licenses then in their power. Note the limit in the text: agencies must weigh military training, but the act does not force them to accept it.
plaw-112-148-2012:
The Raoul Wallenberg Centennial Celebration Act is Public Law 112-148, approved on July 26, 2012. It awards a Congressional Gold Medal to Raoul Wallenberg for his achievements and heroic actions during the Holocaust.

The findings sketch his path. Born in Sweden on August 4, 1912, he graduated from the University of Michigan in 1935, finishing a five-year program in three and a half years. Working in Haifa in 1936, he met young Jews who had fled Nazi persecution in Germany, and their stories moved him deeply. The findings then turn to the War Refugee Board, set up in January 1944 to aid victims of the Axis powers.
plaw-112-149-2012:
Public Law 112-149 is the Insular Areas Act of 2011, approved on July 26, 2012. Its stated aim is to improve the administration of federal programs in the insular areas of the United States.

The section shown in the sample orders continued monitoring on Runit Island in the Marshall Islands. Starting January 1, 2012, the Secretary of Energy must, at least every four years, make a visual study of the concrete shell of the Cactus Crater containment structure. The Secretary must also test the groundwater in and around the structure for radioactive chemicals, and report the results to two named House and Senate committees.
plaw-112-150-2012:
The United States-Israel Enhanced Security Cooperation Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-150, approved on July 27, 2012. It aims to deepen strategic work between the United States and Israel.

The findings frame the case. They recall a special bond between the two countries since 1948, backed by presidents and Congress on a bipartisan basis. They describe a Middle East in rapid change, and they accuse Iran of stirring instability, backing extremism, and enriching uranium against United Nations Security Council rulings. They warn that a nuclear-weapons capable Iran would threaten both countries, and they count more than 60,000 rockets held by Hizbollah and Hamas for use against Israel.
plaw-112-151-2012:
The HEARTH Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-151, approved on July 30, 2012. Its full name is the Helping Expedite and Advance Responsible Tribal Home Ownership Act. It amends a 1955 law on leasing restricted Indian lands for homes, businesses, schools, and other long-term uses.

The point is to let Indian tribes enter certain leases without first gaining express approval from the Secretary of the Interior. The sample text widens older wording that named only the Navajo Nation. Phrases about the Navajo Nation become references to an applicable Indian tribe, and Navajo Nation law becomes applicable tribal law.
plaw-112-152-2012:
The National Baseball Hall of Fame Commemorative Coin Act is Public Law 112-152, approved on August 3, 2012. It requires the Secretary of the Treasury to mint coins in recognition and celebration of the National Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, New York.

The findings praise the museum. It opened on June 12, 1939, with a first class of Ty Cobb, Walter Johnson, Christy Mathewson, Babe Ruth, and Honus Wagner. Just one percent of major league players have earned a place since. The collection holds more than 38,000 artifacts, 3,000,000 documents, and 500,000 photographs, and over 14,000,000 fans have visited since 1939.
plaw-112-153-2012:
The Pilot's Bill of Rights is Public Law 112-153, approved on August 3, 2012. It amends title 49 of the United States Code to give pilots fairer treatment when the Federal Aviation Administration moves against an airman certificate.

Enforcement cases on denial, suspension, or revocation of a certificate are to follow the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and the Federal Rules of Evidence, to the extent practicable. The Administrator must give timely written notice to a pilot under investigation. The notice must say that a reply to a Letter of Investigation is not required, that silence draws no adverse inference, and that any reply may be used as evidence.
plaw-112-154-2012:
Public Law 112-154 is the Honoring America's Veterans and Caring for Camp Lejeune Families Act of 2012, approved on August 6, 2012. It amends title 38 to give hospital care and medical services to veterans who were stationed at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina, while the water there was contaminated. It also aims to improve housing help for veterans and their families.

Title I covers health care matters. Its listed sections include the Camp Lejeune care rule, waivers of copayments for telehealth visits, travel payments for care at Vet Centers, and nursing home care contracts. Others cover sexual assault reporting, brain injury rehabilitation, service dogs on department property, and rural health centers.
plaw-112-155-2012: The Sequestration Transparency Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-155, approved on August 7, 2012. It requires the President to send Congress a detailed report on the spending cuts, called the sequester, set by the Budget Control Act of 2011 for January 2, 2013. The report is due within 30 days of enactment. For discretionary spending it must estimate the cut rates and amounts by category, name each account to be cut, and show the effects at the program, project, and activity level.
plaw-112-156-2012: Public Law 112-156, approved on August 10, 2012, names a post office in Hartshorne, Oklahoma. The Postal Service facility at 1021 Pennsylvania Avenue is to carry the name Warren Lindley Post Office. Its references clause makes any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record count as a mention of the Warren Lindley Post Office. The designation clause in the enacted text omits the usual verb phrase, but the intent is plain from the act's title and structure.
plaw-112-157-2012: Public Law 112-157, approved on August 10, 2012, hands a membership question back to a Texas tribe. It amends the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo and Alabama and Coushatta Indian Tribes of Texas Restoration Act. Section 108(a)(2) now reads that membership covers any person of Tigua Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Indian blood enrolled by the tribe. In plain terms, the Ysleta del Sur Pueblo Tribe itself sets the blood quantum requirement for its own membership.
plaw-112-158-2012:
The Iran Threat Reduction and Syria Human Rights Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-158, approved on August 10, 2012. Its stated purpose is to strengthen Iran sanctions laws so as to compel Iran to give up its pursuit of nuclear weapons and other threatening acts.

Title I deals with expanding the multilateral sanctions regime against Iran, through enforcement and diplomacy. Title II expands sanctions tied to Iran's energy sector and to its work on weapons of mass destruction. Its subtitles widen the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996. They add sanctions on the shipping of crude oil from Iran, and on evasion by shipping firms. They also change the waiver standard under that older act.
plaw-112-159-2012: Public Law 112-159, approved on August 10, 2012, names a post office building in Tampa, Florida for a reverend. The Postal Service facility at 2810 East Hillsborough Avenue is to be known as the Reverend Abe Brown Post Office Building. The references clause adds that any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-160-2012: Public Law 112-160, approved on August 10, 2012, names a post office building in Abbeville, Louisiana for a sergeant. The Postal Service facility at 1421 Veterans Memorial Drive is to be known as the Sergeant Richard Franklin Abshire Post Office Building. Under the references clause, any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-161-2012: Public Law 112-161, approved on August 10, 2012, names a post office in Rome City, Indiana. The Postal Service facility at 125 Kerr Avenue is to be known as the SPC Nicholas Scott Hartge Post Office. Its references clause says any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the SPC Nicholas Scott Hartge Post Office.
plaw-112-162-2012: Public Law 112-162, approved on August 10, 2012, names a post office building in Canton, Mississippi for a first sergeant. The Postal Service facility at 150 South Union Street is to be known as the First Sergeant Landres Cheeks Post Office Building. The references clause makes any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record count as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-163-2012:
Public Law 112-163, approved on August 10, 2012, is headed African Growth and Opportunity Amendments. It extends that trade act's third-country fabric program by swapping 2015 for 2012 in three places. It also adds the Republic of South Sudan to the list of countries that may gain designation under the act, listed right after South Africa.

Section 2 turns to the Dominican Republic-Central America-United States Free Trade Agreement, changing the textile and apparel rules of origin. The act's full purpose line also covers technical corrections to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule and approval of renewed import restrictions under the Burmese Freedom and Democracy Act of 2003.
plaw-112-164-2012: The La Pine Land Conveyance Act is Public Law 112-164, approved on August 10, 2012. It directs the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Bureau of Land Management, to convey federal land to Deschutes County or the City of La Pine, without payment. Either one may gain parcels it requests within one year. Parcel A, about 150 acres in the Prineville District, goes to the county, with a Bureau right-of-way kept for a power substation and line. The sample then begins a second parcel of about 750 acres.
plaw-112-165-2012: The Wallowa Forest Service Compound Conveyance Act is Public Law 112-165, approved on August 10, 2012. It requires the Secretary of Agriculture to convey the Wallowa Forest Service Compound to the city of Wallowa, Oregon, if the city asks within one year. The compound is about 1.11 acres at 602 First Street, donated by the city to the Forest Service on March 18, 1936. The transfer is by quitclaim deed, for no payment. As a condition, the city must use the site as a history and culture education center.
plaw-112-166-2012:
The Presidential Appointment Efficiency and Streamlining Act of 2011 is Public Law 112-166, approved on August 10, 2012. Its aim is to cut the number of executive branch jobs that need Senate confirmation, so presidents can fill lesser posts on their own.

Section 2 works agency by agency, striking the phrase "by and with the advice and consent of the Senate" from one law after another. The sample shows the Agriculture items first: the Assistant Secretary of Agriculture for Administration, the Rural Utilities Service Administrator, and posts under the Commodity Credit Corporation Charter Act. The list then moves to Commerce, starting with the chief scientist of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and on to Defense.
plaw-112-167-2012: Public Law 112-167, approved on August 10, 2012, allows battery recharging stations in Senate parking areas on Capitol Grounds. The Architect of the Capitol may build, run, and maintain the stations for privately owned vehicles used by Senators and covered staff. The money comes from Capitol Power Plant funds, on a reimbursable basis, so there is no net cost to the federal government. Vendors may be used on commission. Work may start only after written notice of numbers and sites goes to the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, and that committee approves.
plaw-112-168-2012:
The Haqqani Network Terrorist Designation Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-168, approved on August 10, 2012. It requires a report on naming the Haqqani Network a foreign terrorist organization.

The findings cite a research report on the network. Led by Jalaluddin Haqqani and his son Sirajuddin from the tribal areas of Pakistan, it is called the most dangerous Afghan insurgent group fighting United States led forces. They recount 2011 attacks: the June assault on the Intercontinental Hotel in Kabul, and a September truck bomb in Wardak that wounded 77 American troops. A third was a 20-hour gun battle at the embassy in Kabul. Admiral Mullen is quoted calling the network a veritable arm of Pakistan's intelligence agency.
plaw-112-169-2012: Public Law 112-169, approved on August 10, 2012, widens the uses of coin money for an infantry museum. It amends section 6(b) of the National Infantry Museum and Soldier Center Commemorative Coin Act, Public Law 110-357. After the existing list of uses for the coin surcharges, it adds one more purpose: the retirement of debt tied to building the existing National Infantry Museum and Soldier Center. The whole act is that single insertion.
plaw-112-170-2012: Public Law 112-170, approved on August 16, 2012, is the House twin of a Senate measure passed days earlier. It lets the Architect of the Capitol build, run, and maintain battery recharging stations in House parking areas on Capitol Grounds. The work runs on a reimbursable basis, at no net cost to the federal government. The stations serve privately owned vehicles of House members, delegates, the Resident Commissioner, and covered staff. Vendors may serve on commission. Work needs written notice to, and approval by, the Committee on House Administration.
plaw-112-171-2012: Public Law 112-171, approved on August 16, 2012, brings one agency under a veterans job rights law. It amends the Aviation and Transportation Security Act so the Under Secretary, in carrying out screening functions, is subject to chapter 43 of title 38. That chapter is the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act, which guards the jobs of workers called to military service. The change takes effect 270 days after enactment, so in plain terms the Transportation Security Administration must comply with that act.
plaw-112-172-2012:
Public Law 112-172 is the Ambassador James R. Lilley and Congressman Stephen J. Solarz North Korea Human Rights Reauthorization Act of 2012, approved on August 16, 2012. It reauthorizes the North Korean Human Rights Act of 2004.

The findings say the 2004 act and its 2008 renewal rested on broad bipartisan agreement on human rights, open aid delivery, and refugee protection. They note that Kim Jong-Un's rise after the death of Kim Jong-Il brought new uncertainty, yet rights and aid conditions inside North Korea remain deplorable and refugees remain at great risk. Reports of a crackdown on border crossing during the change of rule are also cited.
plaw-112-173-2012: Public Law 112-173, approved on August 16, 2012, delays parts of the STOCK Act to guard national security and protect covered officers and staff. It strikes August 31, 2012 and inserts September 30, 2012 in two sections of that act, sections 8(a)(1) and 11(a)(1), which deal with putting financial reports online. A second section shapes how the periodic transaction report rules apply to filers who report to the Clerk of the House. From September 30, 2012, it ties them to the transaction data those rules require.
plaw-112-174-2012:
Public Law 112-174, approved on September 20, 2012, directs the Joint Committee on the Library to accept a statue of Frederick Douglass from the District of Columbia. The statue is to stand on permanent display in Emancipation Hall of the United States Capitol.

The findings honor Douglass's life. Born Frederick Augustus Washington Bailey in Maryland in 1818, he escaped slavery and became a leading writer, speaker, and publisher for abolition, women's suffrage, and the equality of all people. He lived 25 years in Rochester, New York, where he published The North Star. His 1845 autobiography was a best seller, and in the Civil War he recruited Black soldiers, two of them his own sons.
plaw-112-175-2012:
Public Law 112-175 is the Continuing Appropriations Resolution, 2013, approved on September 28, 2012. As a joint resolution, it keeps the federal government funded into fiscal year 2013 before the regular spending bills for that year were in place.

Section 101 continues projects and activities run in fiscal year 2012, at a rate of operations drawn from the 2012 spending acts and under their terms. The list begins with the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration act, then the Commerce, Justice, and Science act, the Defense act, and the Energy and Water act. Disaster relief items named in the 2012 acts are carved out of the first two entries.
plaw-112-176-2012: Public Law 112-176, approved on September 28, 2012, extends four immigration programs by three years each. Every end date of September 30, 2012 becomes September 30, 2015. The programs are the EB-5 Regional Center Program, the E-Verify Program, the Special Immigrant Nonminister Religious Worker Program, and the Conrad State 30 J-1 Visa Waiver Program. For the EB-5 program, the act also strikes the word "pilot" wherever it appears. A final section bars any reading of the act that would allow work on a national identification card.
plaw-112-177-2012: The Pesticide Registration Improvement Extension Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-177, approved on September 28, 2012. It reauthorizes the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act, the main federal law on pesticide registration. The sample text resets the maintenance fees firms pay. The total amount is set at $27,800,000 for each of the fiscal years 2013 through 2017. Other per-firm sums in the sample are set at $115,500 and $184,800 for those same years, with further fee figures following in the same section.
plaw-112-178-2012: Public Law 112-178, approved on September 28, 2012, moves the start date for putting STOCK Act disclosure forms on the internet. For most filers, sections 8(a)(1) and 11(a)(1) of the STOCK Act take effect on December 8, 2012. The date does not apply to forms from the President, the Vice President, members and candidates for Congress, or Senate-confirmed officers in the top pay levels of title 5. Within 30 days, the Office of Personnel Management must hire the National Academy of Public Administration to study online posting and report back.
plaw-112-179-2012:
The Minnesota Chippewa Tribe Judgment Fund Distribution Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-179, approved on October 5, 2012. It provides for the use and payout of funds awarded to the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe by the United States Court of Federal Claims in Docket Numbers 19 and 188.

The findings trace the claims back decades. The tribe filed Docket 19 in 1948, seeking an accounting under the Nelson Act of 1889, and Docket 188 in 1951 for duties under other statutes and treaties. A settlement won court approval, final judgment came on May 26, 1999, and $20,000,000 moved to a trust fund at the Interior Department that June.
plaw-112-180-2012: Public Law 112-180, approved on October 5, 2012, names a courthouse still being built in Fort Pierce, Florida. The United States courthouse under construction at 101 South United States Route 1 is to be known as the Alto Lee Adams, Sr., United States Courthouse. The references section makes any mention of that courthouse in a federal law, map, rule, or record count as a mention of the Alto Lee Adams, Sr., United States Courthouse.
plaw-112-181-2012:
The Lions Clubs International Century of Service Commemorative Coin Act is Public Law 112-181, approved on October 5, 2012. It requires the Secretary of the Treasury to mint coins marking one hundred years since Lions Clubs International was founded.

The findings honor that record. Chicago business leader Melvin Jones founded the group in 1917, and it grew into the world's largest service club body, with over 1.35 million members in more than 45,000 clubs. In 1945 it helped draft the United Nations Charter. Its foundation, set up in 1968, has given more than $700 million for sight, health, youth, disability, and disaster relief work.
plaw-112-182-2012: The Lowell National Historical Park Land Exchange Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-182, approved on October 5, 2012. It amends the 1978 act that set up Lowell National Historical Park in Massachusetts. The Secretary may swap park land with the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, the city of Lowell, or the University of Massachusetts Building Authority. Swaps follow Park Service rules and the Secretary's terms. If park facilities stand on the federal land and the values differ, the gap is closed by a cash payment to the Secretary.
plaw-112-183-2012:
The Billfish Conservation Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-183, approved on October 5, 2012. Its purpose line is blunt: to prohibit the sale of billfish. Congress finds that global billfish stocks have fallen sharply, mainly because foreign fleets keep billfish caught as bycatch.

The ban bars any person from offering for sale, selling, or holding for sale billfish or products containing billfish. A breach is punished under the Magnuson-Stevens fishery law. One exemption protects old markets: billfish caught by United States vessels and landed in Hawaii or the Pacific Insular Areas may still be sold.
plaw-112-184-2012: Public Law 112-184, approved on October 5, 2012, names the new United States courthouse in Buffalo, New York. The courthouse at 2 Niagara Square is to be known as the Robert H. Jackson United States Courthouse. Section 2 adds the references rule, so any mention of that courthouse in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the Robert H. Jackson United States Courthouse.
plaw-112-185-2012:
Public Law 112-185, approved on October 5, 2012, confirms that early American astronauts own the small flight items they kept. A United States astronaut from the Mercury, Gemini, or Apollo programs, through the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project, holds full ownership and clear title to artifacts received during the program.

The act defines artifacts as expendable or personal-use items NASA did not require back, including personal logs, checklists, flight manuals, training test pieces, and disposable flight hardware saved from jettisoned lunar modules. Lunar rocks and other lunar material are left out. The federal government may make no ownership claim, even over items later sold to a third party.
plaw-112-186-2012:
The SAFE DOSES Act is Public Law 112-186, approved on October 5, 2012. Its long name, Strengthening and Focusing Enforcement to Deter Organized Stealing and Enhance Safety, states the aim: stop the theft of medical products by amending title 18 of the United States Code.

The act adds section 670, which makes it a crime to steal, embezzle, or by fraud obtain a pre-retail medical product in interstate or foreign commerce. It also bans forging labels or shipping papers for such goods, and holding, moving, or trafficking in goods tied to those crimes. Buying or selling expired or stolen medical products with intent to defraud is banned as well, along with attempts and conspiracies.
plaw-112-187-2012: Public Law 112-187, approved on October 5, 2012, names a courthouse in Juneau, Alaska. The United States courthouse at 709 West 9th Street is to be known as the Robert Boochever United States Courthouse. The references section adds that any mention of that courthouse in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the Robert Boochever United States Courthouse.
plaw-112-188-2012: The Divisional Realignment Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-188, approved on October 5, 2012. It redraws division lines inside two federal judicial districts by amending title 28 of the United States Code. In the Eastern District of Missouri, Iron County and Saint Genevieve County move from one division's county list to another. The Northern District of Mississippi is restated as three divisions: Aberdeen, Oxford, and Greenville, each with its own county list and court towns. The changes take effect 60 days after enactment.
plaw-112-189-2012: The Reporting Efficiency Improvement Act is Public Law 112-189, approved on October 5, 2012. Its goal is to drop needless reporting duties for unfunded programs under the Office of Justice Programs. For DNA identification grants, it strikes the subsection that required reports to the Attorney General. For the Police Corps program, it repeals the report requirement in section 200113 of the Police Corps Act outright. It also strikes that section's line from the table of contents of the Violent Crime Control and Law Enforcement Act of 1994.
plaw-112-190-2012: Public Law 112-190, approved on October 5, 2012, fixes an error in the Trademark Act of 1946, in the part on remedies for dilution. It rewrites two subparagraphs of section 43(c)(6). The new text covers a suit brought by another person under the common law or a state statute. It must either seek to stop dilution by blurring or by tarnishment, or claim actual or likely harm to the distinctiveness or reputation of a mark, label, or form of advertisement. The fix applies to suits begun on or after enactment.
plaw-112-191-2012:
The VA Major Construction Authorization and Expiring Authorities Extension Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-191, approved on October 5, 2012. It authorizes major medical facility projects for the Department of Veterans Affairs and keeps a set of expiring powers of the Secretary alive.

Title I authorizes the fiscal year 2013 major medical facility projects, a further project in Miami, Florida, and the funds for them. Title II extends listed powers. They include working out the net value of property behind a defaulted loan. They also include running the VA office in Manila in the Philippines, and services for seriously mentally ill and homeless veterans.
plaw-112-192-2012:
Public Law 112-192, approved on October 5, 2012, gives the United States room to back aid for Burma through world lenders. If the President finds it in the national interest, the Secretary of the Treasury may give an order. The order tells the United States Executive Director at any international financial institution to vote for the institution's assistance to Burma, despite any other law.

The act adds safeguards. The Secretaries of State and the Treasury must first consult the named House and Senate committees on the aid and the interests it serves. The President must give those committees written notice, and no vote in favor may come until at least 15 days after that notice. Assistance means any loan or aid of funds.
plaw-112-193-2012: The FDA User Fee Corrections Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-193, approved on October 5, 2012. It makes repairs to the Food and Drug Administration user fee rules in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. One fix swaps a cross-reference, from 744A(a)(4) to 744B(a)(4). Another softens "shall only be available" to "shall be available", and a third adds the words "for such year" after "obligation of fees" in four places. Punctuation is corrected in one date clause. The act sets due dates for two fiscal year 2013 fees.
plaw-112-194-2012:
The Government Charge Card Abuse Prevention Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-194, approved on October 5, 2012. It aims to stop misuse of government purchase cards and convenience checks by tightening agency controls.

New section 1909 of title 41 orders each agency head to keep safeguards and internal controls. Each card holder must be listed in agency records, along with the limits on single and total transactions for that card. Each holder needs an approving official who is not the holder. Holders and officials must match charges on each statement against receipts and other papers, and send a summary report to the certifying official, so the government pays only valid charges.
plaw-112-195-2012:
The Hazardous Waste Electronic Manifest Establishment Act is Public Law 112-195, approved on October 5, 2012. It amends the Solid Waste Disposal Act to direct the head of the Environmental Protection Agency to build an electronic manifest system for hazardous waste.

New section 3024 sets up the frame. It defines an advisory board, a fund, and the system itself. A user is a hazardous waste generator, a transporter, or the owner or operator of a treatment, storage, recycling, or disposal site, plus anyone else who must use a manifest. Manifests track waste shipments from the place it is made to an off-site facility that treats, stores, or discards it.
plaw-112-196-2012: The Military Commercial Driver's License Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-196, approved on October 19, 2012. It amends section 31311 of title 49, which normally lets a state issue a commercial driver's license only to a person domiciled there. The act adds an exception for service members whose duty station is in the state but are not domiciled there. Covered members serve in the active duty military, the reserves, the National Guard, the active duty Coast Guard, or the Coast Guard Auxiliary, and run a commercial motor vehicle.
plaw-112-197-2012: The New York City Natural Gas Supply Enhancement Act is Public Law 112-197, approved on November 27, 2012. It lets the Secretary of the Interior permit the Transcontinental Gas Pipeline Company, or Transco, to build and run a natural gas pipeline in the Gateway National Recreation Area in New York. Permits must match the laws for utility rights-of-way in park units, plus any terms the Secretary sets. The fee rests on fair market value and repays Park Service costs of processing, issuing, and watching the permit.
plaw-112-198-2012: The Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-198, approved on November 27, 2012. Effective December 1, 2012, the Secretary of Veterans Affairs must raise the dollar amounts in force on November 30, 2012 for disability compensation and for dependency and indemnity compensation. The amounts to be raised cover wartime disability compensation, extra pay for dependents, the clothing allowance, and survivors' pay for a spouse and for children. Each amount rises by the same percentage the act ties to benefit amounts in its next clause.
plaw-112-199-2012:
The Whistleblower Protection Enhancement Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-199, approved on November 27, 2012. It amends chapter 23 of title 5 to strengthen the guard federal workers gain when they disclose wrongdoing.

The stated aims include clarifying which disclosures are protected from prohibited personnel practices. They also include a rule that non-disclosure policies, forms, and agreements must state that they conform with the disclosure protections, and new authority for the Special Counsel. Title I, on protection of certain disclosures, begins by widening section 2302(b)(8): the words "a violation" become "any violation" in the clauses shown.
plaw-112-200-2012: The European Union Emissions Trading Scheme Prohibition Act of 2011 is Public Law 112-200, approved on November 27, 2012. It directs the Secretary of Transportation to bar operators of United States civil aircraft from taking part in the European Union's emissions trading scheme, under EU Directive 2003/87/EC. The bar may be imposed when the Secretary finds it in the public interest, weighing effects on American consumers and carriers, on economic, energy, and environmental security, and on foreign relations. A public hearing must come at least 30 days before a bar.
plaw-112-201-2012:
The Mark Twain Commemorative Coin Act is Public Law 112-201, approved on December 4, 2012. It requires the Secretary of the Treasury to mint coins in commemoration of Mark Twain, the pen name of Samuel Clemens.

The findings praise his reach. More than 6,500 editions of his books have been translated into 75 languages. Books such as The Adventures of Tom Sawyer and Adventures of Huckleberry Finn have never gone out of print. In two decades, over 100 books and 250 doctoral dissertations treated his life and work. The findings note his themes: the legacy of the Civil War, race relations, and the wealth gaps of the Gilded Age.
plaw-112-202-2012: The Taking Essential Steps for Testing Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-202, approved on December 4, 2012. It amends section 353 of the Public Health Service Act, the laboratory certification section. One change bars a lab from sending a proficiency testing sample to another lab for analysis, as a separate clause already forbids. Another lets the Secretary use intermediate sanctions instead of the two-year ban on owning or running a lab, when a certificate is revoked for such a breach. A last change swaps "shall" for "may" there.
plaw-112-203-2012: Public Law 112-203, approved on December 4, 2012, extends the U.S. SAFE WEB Act of 2006. That law, whose long name is the Undertaking Spam, Spyware, And Fraud Enforcement With Enforcers beyond Borders Act, backs federal work against online fraud across borders. This act rewrites its sunset section. The 2006 act and its amendments are now repealed effective September 30, 2020, and the laws it changed are then read as if it had never been enacted.
plaw-112-204-2012:
Public Law 112-204, approved on December 4, 2012, consolidates some Congressional Budget Office reporting duties tied to two crisis-era laws. For the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009, the office's comments on all quarterly reports for a year are due 45 days after the last quarter's report is sent. That comment rule is itself repealed on January 1, 2016.

For the Troubled Asset Relief Program, under the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008, the reporting cycle drops from twice a year to once a year. The duty ends after the annual period in which the last troubled assets the Treasury bought have been sold or moved out of federal hands.
plaw-112-205-2012:
The Jaime Zapata Border Enforcement Security Task Force Act is Public Law 112-205, approved on December 7, 2012. It sets up a Border Enforcement Security Task Force program to guard American border towns from cross-border crime, including drug trafficking, arms smuggling, human smuggling, violence, and kidnapping.

The findings explain the model. Crime and violence surged on Mexico's northern border as drug cartels fought each other, and northern border officers face smuggling groups as well. In reply, the Department of Homeland Security had already formed BEST teams, joining federal, state, local, tribal, and foreign officers. The teams share information and work cases together, with Immigration and Customs Enforcement in a lead role.
plaw-112-206-2012:
The Child Protection Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-206, approved on December 7, 2012. It amends title 18 of the United States Code on child pornography and child exploitation offenses.

Section 2 raises penalties for possession. When the material in the offense involves a prepubescent minor, or a minor under 12 years of age, the person faces a fine and up to 20 years in prison. The same added wording goes into two sections, 2252 and 2252A. Section 3 turns to child witnesses. It reshapes the civil action used to restrain harassment of a victim or witness. The court may act on its own motion, and minor witnesses gain a protective order rule.
plaw-112-207-2012: Public Law 112-207, approved on December 7, 2012, changes one date in an act passed that same fall. Public Law 112-178 had set December 8, 2012 as the start date for putting certain STOCK Act financial disclosure forms on the internet. This act strikes that date and inserts April 15, 2013. The swap itself takes effect on December 8, 2012, the day the posting was to have begun.
plaw-112-208-2012:
Public Law 112-208 is the Russia and Moldova Jackson-Vanik Repeal and Sergei Magnitsky Rule of Law Accountability Act of 2012, approved on December 14, 2012. It authorizes normal trade relations treatment for products of the Russian Federation and Moldova, and calls for reports on how Russia meets its World Trade Organization duties.

Title I grants permanent normal trade relations for Russia, ending the use of title IV of the Trade Act of 1974 for Russian goods. Title II lists trade enforcement steps. It calls for reports on Russia's carrying out of its trade duties, and on enforcement work by the United States Trade Representative. It also calls for reports on Russian rules that discriminate against American digital goods.
plaw-112-209-2012:
The March of Dimes Commemorative Coin Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-209, approved on December 18, 2012. It requires the Secretary of the Treasury to mint coins marking the 75th anniversary of the March of Dimes Foundation.

The findings tell the foundation's story. President Franklin Roosevelt, who himself fought polio, created the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis on January 3, 1938. It funded the polio vaccines of Jonas Salk and Albert Sabin; the Salk vaccine was tested in 1954 on 1.8 million schoolchildren, the polio pioneers, and licensed in 1955. With polio beaten, the group turned in 1958 to birth defects, early birth, and infant deaths.
plaw-112-210-2012: The American Energy Manufacturing Technical Corrections Act is Public Law 112-210, approved on December 18, 2012. It makes technical corrections to energy efficiency laws, so makers can use new designs that meet or beat the energy goals and stay competitive. Section 2 covers innovative parts for walk-in coolers and freezers. A part maker escapes one rule if it shows the Secretary that its part cuts energy use at least as much as the rule would, backed by full data. Section 3 begins a uniform efficiency descriptor for covered water heaters.
plaw-112-211-2012:
The Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-211, approved on December 18, 2012. It carries out two treaties in United States law: the Hague Agreement on the international registration of industrial designs, and the Patent Law Treaty.

Title I adds a new Part V to title 35 of the United States Code, with a chapter 38 on international design applications. The listed sections define terms and set rules for filing such applications, their filing date, and their legal effect. They also cover priority rights, relief from missed time limits, withdrawn applications, examination, and publication of the application.
plaw-112-212-2012: The Bridgeport Indian Colony Land Trust, Health, and Economic Development Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-212, approved on December 20, 2012. It declares about 39.36 acres of federal land in Mono County, California to be held in trust for the Bridgeport Indian Colony. One parcel of 7.5 acres is shown on a 2010 map as the Bridgeport Camp Antelope Parcel. The second, 31.86 acres, rests on a 2003 survey plat near State Highway 182. Easements and rights-of-way in place stay valid.
plaw-112-213-2012:
The Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-213, approved on December 20, 2012. It authorizes appropriations for the Coast Guard for fiscal years 2013 and 2014.

Title I holds the authorization itself, plus the approved levels of military strength and training. Title II is a long list of Coast Guard rules. The contents shown cover interference with Coast Guard transmissions, care and use of Coast Guard assets, spending limits, Academy pay, and a policy on sexual harassment and sexual violence. Further listed items include officer appointments and selection boards, major acquisitions, advance procurement funding, and capital investment planning.
plaw-112-214-2012: Public Law 112-214, approved on December 20, 2012, lets the Pascua Yaqui Tribe set its own membership rules. It rewrites section 3 of Public Law 95-375 to say that membership of the tribe consists of any United States citizen of Pascua Yaqui blood enrolled by the tribe. The requirements for membership are thus determined by the tribe itself, through whom it enrolls.
plaw-112-215-2012: Public Law 112-215, approved on December 20, 2012, amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act on information given to the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection. In section 11(t)(2)(A), the Bureau is added as a new listed recipient, clause (vi). In section 18(x), the Bureau's name is inserted before "any Federal banking agency" wherever that phrase appears, and "such agency" becomes "such Bureau, agency" in the same places. The edits place the Bureau inside the Act's information-sharing rules.
plaw-112-216-2012: Public Law 112-216, approved on December 20, 2012, trims a notice rule for cash machines. It amends the Electronic Fund Transfer Act, section 904(d)(3)(B) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act. The change limits the fee disclosure duty for an automatic teller machine to the screen of that machine. The edits rewrite the notice clause and cut off a trailing passage that began with an exception tied to a time period. What survives is the on-screen notice requirement in clauses (i) and (ii).
plaw-112-217-2012: The DART Act, or DHS Audit Requirement Target Act of 2012, is Public Law 112-217, approved on December 20, 2012. Its aim is to gain a clean, unqualified audit opinion for the Department of Homeland Security and to improve the department's money management. The Secretary must take the steps needed so the department's full consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2013, and each year after, are ready in time for audit. The related reports are due by November 15, 2013 and each year after that.
plaw-112-218-2012: The No-Hassle Flying Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-218, approved on December 20, 2012. It adds a preclearance paragraph to section 44901(d) of title 49. For such flights, the head of the Transportation Security Administration may make a call. Bags screened under a security preclearance pact with that country may not need a second screening. Working with Customs and Border Protection, the TSA head decides if the bags need screening again by an explosives detection system before onward flights. Such pacts set standards judged comparable to United States ones.
plaw-112-219-2012: Public Law 112-219, approved on December 28, 2012, names a post office building in Crosby, Texas for an Army first sergeant. The Postal Service facility at 133 Hare Road is to be known as the Army First Sergeant David McNerney Post Office Building. The references clause makes any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record count as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-220-2012:
The Countering Iran in the Western Hemisphere Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-220, approved on December 28, 2012. It calls for a comprehensive strategy against Iran's growing hostile presence and activity in the Americas.

The findings say Iran signs economic and security deals with Latin American countries to soften sanctions and block Western pressure. They name Hezbollah, backed by Iran, as the most technically capable terrorist group in the world, with thousands of supporters and members. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Qods Force is said to fund, arm, and guide Hezbollah, and to place operatives in embassies, charities, and cultural bodies across Latin America.
plaw-112-221-2012: Public Law 112-221, approved on December 28, 2012, names a post office in Rose Bud, Arkansas. The Postal Service facility at 6083 Highway 36 West is to be known as the Nicky 'Nick' Daniel Bacon Post Office. Its references clause says any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of the Nicky 'Nick' Daniel Bacon Post Office.
plaw-112-222-2012: Public Law 112-222, approved on December 28, 2012, names a post office building in Mastic Beach, New York for a brigadier general. The Postal Service facility at 110 Mastic Road is to be known as the Brigadier General Nathaniel Woodhull Post Office Building. The references clause adds that any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-223-2012: Public Law 112-223, approved on December 28, 2012, names a postal facility in Macomb, Michigan. The facility at 15285 Samohin Drive is to be known as the Lance Cpl. Anthony A. DiLisio Clinton-Macomb Carrier Annex. Note that this is a carrier annex, not a post office building. The references clause makes any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record count as a mention of the full annex name.
plaw-112-224-2012: Public Law 112-224, approved on December 28, 2012, names a post office building in Baldwinsville, New York for a corporal. The Postal Service facility at 26 East Genesee Street is to be known as the Corporal Kyle Schneider Post Office Building. Its references clause says any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-225-2012: Public Law 112-225, approved on December 28, 2012, names a post office building in Ellwood City, Pennsylvania for a sergeant. The Postal Service facility at 320 7th Street is to be known as the Sergeant Leslie H. Sabo, Jr. Post Office Building. The references clause adds that any mention of that facility in a federal law, map, rule, or record counts as a mention of that building name.
plaw-112-226-2012: Public Law 112-226, approved on December 28, 2012, opens a direct path from the Virgin Islands' top court to the nation's. It amends the Revised Organic Act of the Virgin Islands and adds section 1260 to title 28. That court's final judgments may be reviewed by the United States Supreme Court by writ of certiorari. Review lies where a federal treaty's or statute's validity is in question, where an island statute is attacked as repugnant to federal law, or where a right is claimed under the Constitution.
plaw-112-227-2012: Public Law 112-227, approved on December 28, 2012, clarifies a naturalization rule for support staff working abroad. It rewrites part of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2006. Time spent outside the United States in a job for the Chief of Mission or the Armed Forces does not break continuous residence for naturalization. This holds for work under contract with them, in posts such as translator, interpreter, or a security-related executive or managerial post. That time counts as residence and physical presence in the United States.
plaw-112-228-2012: Public Law 112-228 is a joint resolution, approved on December 28, 2012, that sets a date in the presidential election process. The electors cast their votes for President and Vice President in December 2012. Under section 15 of title 3, the Senate and House meet in January 2013 to count those electoral votes. This resolution fixes that meeting on January 4, 2013, rather than the date the statute's first sentence would otherwise give.
plaw-112-229-2012:
The D.C. Courts and Public Defender Service Act of 2011 is Public Law 112-229, approved on December 28, 2012. It revises administrative powers of the District of Columbia courts under title 11 of the District's code. It also authorizes the Public Defender Service to buy professional liability insurance. The insurance covers its officers and staff, for claims tied to work within their jobs.

The sample shows the courts part. The judicial conference may meet biennially or annually, and magistrate judges now attend and share the duties judges held. A new section gives emergency power to toll or delay Superior Court proceedings when a natural disaster or other emergency closes the court or makes deadlines impracticable.
plaw-112-230-2012:
The Hatch Act Modernization Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-230, approved on December 28, 2012. It scales back the Hatch Act rule that barred many state and local workers from running for elective office. It clarifies how the act treats the District of Columbia, and changes penalties for some breaches.

Section 2 rewrites the candidacy ban in section 1502(a)(3) of title 5. A state or local employee is now barred from candidacy only when the salary is paid completely, directly or indirectly, by loans or grants from the United States or a federal agency. Section 3 folds the executive branch of the District of Columbia into the definition of a state or local agency.
plaw-112-231-2012: The 21st Century Language Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-231, approved on December 28, 2012. Its job is to strike the word "lunatic" from federal law. In title 1, the word is cut from the list of terms on number and gender. In banking law, the trust powers act loses the phrase "committee of estates of lunatics". In the National Bank Consolidation and Merger Act, lists naming such a committee are cut, leaving the receiver alone. Its heading calls this modernizing language for persons who are mentally ill.
plaw-112-232-2012:
The Barona Band of Mission Indians Land Transfer Clarification Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-232, approved on December 28, 2012. It makes technical corrections to the legal description of land held in trust for the Barona Band of Mission Indians.

Congress finds that the old description may be read to cover private, nontribal land. The purposes are to clarify the 2004 trust description and remove all doubt about which parcels Congress placed in trust. The findings note a live dispute with off-reservation owners over falling native groundwater. Congress states that it takes no side in it. The findings also set a water condition for any project that brings water to the reservation.
plaw-112-233-2012: Public Law 112-233, approved on December 28, 2012, moves a courthouse name in Billings, Montana. The United States courthouse at 2601 2nd Avenue North is to be known as the James F. Battin United States Courthouse. A technical amendment adds that the building at 315 North 26th Street, which had carried that name, shall no longer be known by it. The references clause then ties federal mentions of the 2nd Avenue courthouse to the Battin name.
plaw-112-234-2012: The GAO Mandates Revision Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-234, approved on December 28, 2012. It repeals or softens certain duties laid on the Government Accountability Office. Capitol Preservation Fund statements move from annual audits to periodic audits, at least once every three years, or sooner on request by named officers. The act strikes a subsection that required a GAO audit for the Judicial Survivors' Annuities Fund. The drug control office report becomes due December 31, 2013, and every three years after.
plaw-112-235-2012: The Public Interest Declassification Board Reauthorization Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-235, approved on December 28, 2012. It extends the Public Interest Declassification Act of 2000 to 2014, swapping that year for 2012 in its sunset clause. Two smaller edits shape board terms. A clause on later appointments is completed with the words "from the date of the appointment". The sentence saying a member named to fill a vacancy serves the rest of the term is struck from the vacancy rule.
plaw-112-236-2012: The Theft of Trade Secrets Clarification Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-236, approved on December 28, 2012. It clarifies the reach of the Economic Espionage Act of 1996 by editing one clause in section 1832(a) of title 18. Out go the words tying a case to a secret "included in a product that is produced for or placed in" commerce. In their place, the text covers a secret tied to "a product or service used in or intended for use in" commerce. That wording is the whole act.
plaw-112-237-2012:
Public Law 112-237, approved on December 28, 2012, pairs a Louisiana water program with two building renamings. It amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to reauthorize the Lake Pontchartrain Basin Restoration Program. Grants under the program may pay not more than 75 percent of costs. Its funding line swaps 2011 for 2012 plus the amount appropriated for fiscal year 2009, for each of fiscal years 2013 through 2017.

Section 2 redesignates the Environmental Protection Agency headquarters in Washington, known as the Ariel Rios Building, as the William Jefferson Clinton Federal Building. Section 3 redesignates the federal building and courthouse in Midland, Texas, known as the George Mahon Federal Building, with a long name honoring George H.W. Bush, George W. Bush, and George Mahon.
plaw-112-238-2012: The FISA Amendments Act Reauthorization Act of 2012 is Public Law 112-238, approved on December 30, 2012. It extends the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 for five years. In section 403(b) of the 2008 act, both mentions of December 31, 2012 become December 31, 2017. A matching change is made to a heading in section 404(b)(1) of the same act. The two date swaps are the substance of the law.
plaw-112-82-2012:
Belarus rights abuses frame Public Law 112-82, the Belarus Democracy and Human Rights Act of 2011. The 112th Congress passed it to renew the Belarus Democracy Act of 2004. It was approved on January 3, 2012. Section 2 rewrites the findings and policy text of the older act.

Congress finds that the Government of Belarus has breached human rights and basic freedoms in a clear, uncorrected pattern. It finds the same pattern in votes that were flawed at their core. Those votes weakened the claim of both branches to lawful power. The findings add that thousands of pro-democracy activists faced harassment, beatings, and jail.
plaw-112-83-2012: Little Ferry, New Jersey, gains a named post office under Public Law 112-83 of the 112th Congress, approved in 2012. The site at 20 Main Street in Little Ferry must be known as the Sergeant Matthew J. Fenton Post Office. Any mention of that site in a federal law, map, rule, record, or other paper counts as a mention of the new name. The act does nothing else.
plaw-112-84-2012: Judges' safety is the aim of Public Law 112-84, approved by the 112th Congress on January 3, 2012. The act extends the power of the Judicial Conference to redact, or black out, touchy facts in judges' financial disclosure reports. It amends section 105 of the Ethics in Government Act of 1978. One fix changes Marshall to Marshals. Two House and Senate panels are added as report readers. The end year moves from 2011 to 2017 in both places it appears.
plaw-112-85-2012: Jackson, Tennessee, gains a named plaza under Public Law 112-85 of the 112th Congress, approved on January 3, 2012. The land between the federal courthouse and the Ed Jones Building at 109 South Highland Avenue becomes the M. D. Anderson Plaza. A marker on the grounds may honor the deeds and giving of M. D. Anderson. Findings say Monroe Dunaway Anderson was born in Jackson in 1873. He grew into a top cotton trader who co-founded Anderson, Clayton, and Company in 1904.
plaw-112-86-2012: Faster airport screening for troops is set up by Public Law 112-86, the Risk-Based Security Screening for Members of the Armed Forces Act. The 112th Congress amended title 49 in early 2012. The head of the Transportation Security Administration must build a plan with the Defense Department. The plan gives fast screening to a member of the armed forces in uniform. The member must show papers for official air travel from a primary airport. Family members who travel with the member are covered where that can be done.
plaw-112-87-2012:
Public Law 112-87, the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2012, was approved on January 3, 2012. The 112th Congress used it to back funds for spy work across the United States Government. It also covers the Community Management Account. A third charge is the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System.

Title I covers the spy work itself. It grants funds, sets a classified schedule of grants, and allows shifts in staff caps. Title II funds the CIA retirement system. Title III holds general rules, starting with raises in worker pay and benefits set by law.
plaw-112-88-2012: One study, and nothing more, is ordered by Public Law 112-88 of the 112th Congress, approved in 2012. The Inspector General of the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation must study the full impact of bank failures. The banks in scope are insured depository institutions, as the Federal Deposit Insurance Act defines them. One topic is loss-sharing deals and their effect. The study asks how those deals affect banks that survive a failure. It also asks how they affect people who borrowed from banks that failed.
plaw-112-89-2012: A Staten Island mail site gains a name under Public Law 112-89, approved by the 112th Congress in 2012. The Postal Service site at 45 Bay Street, Suite 2, in Staten Island, New York, must be known as the Sergeant Angel Mendez Post Office. References to the site in federal laws, maps, rules, records, and other papers count as references to that name.
plaw-112-90-2012: Pipeline safety is tightened by Public Law 112-90, the Pipeline Safety, Regulatory Certainty, and Job Creation Act of 2011. The 112th Congress approved it on January 3, 2012. It amends title 49 of the United States Code. The stated aims are stronger safety and stronger protection of nature in pipeline transport. A third aim is firmer trust in how the nation's energy goods move by pipeline. Most of the sample is framing text and terms drawn from chapter 601 of title 49.
plaw-112-91-2012: Public Law 112-91, the Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2012, buys the airport system about two more weeks. The 112th Congress passed it on January 31, 2012. Fuel taxes and ticket taxes fund the Airport and Airway Trust Fund. Each was set to lapse on January 31, 2012. Section 2 moves each end date to February 17, 2012. The act's head note says it also extends grants for the airport improvement program in title 49.
plaw-112-92-2012: School choice terms are fixed by Public Law 112-92, the SOAR Technical Corrections Act. The 112th Congress passed it in early 2012 to clarify the scope of the SOAR Act. Section 2 rewrites a use-of-funds rule. Students in the program must be taught core school subjects by a teacher with a bachelor's degree or its match. The degree may come from inside or outside the United States. Section 3 then deals with standard tests. The Institute of Education Sciences must give tests that are norm-referenced at the national level.
plaw-112-93-2012: Ultralight smuggling by air is the target of Public Law 112-93, the Ultralight Aircraft Smuggling Prevention Act of 2012, passed by the 112th Congress. It amends the Tariff Act of 1930. The point is to clarify what counts as an aircraft under the aviation smuggling rules. The word takes its title 49 sense and also covers the craft named in a federal flight rule. Those craft are the light vehicles of part 103, such as ultralights. A second part amends the crime terms, reaching attempts as the sample starts to state.
plaw-112-94-2012: Mississippi's Noxubee refuge takes a new name under Public Law 112-94 of the 112th Congress, passed in 2012. The Noxubee National Wildlife Refuge is redesignated as the Sam D. Hamilton Noxubee National Wildlife Refuge. The act bars no other change to the refuge. The Interior Secretary may still adjust its borders as fits the refuge system's mission. The Secretary may also add new land or parcels to the refuge on the same terms.
plaw-112-95-2012:
Public Law 112-95, the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, sets the path of the Federal Aviation Administration for fiscal years 2011 through 2014. The 112th Congress amended title 49 to grant its funds. The stated aims are leaner programs, less waste, and better safety and capacity in flight. Steady funding for the national aviation system is a further aim.

Title I holds the grants of funds. Its first subtitle covers airport planning and growth, air navigation gear, and agency operations. It also marks out projects of the Next Generation Air Transportation System. A later subtitle covers passenger facility charges.
plaw-112-96-2012:
Jobs and tax relief share Public Law 112-96, the Middle Class Tax Relief and Job Creation Act of 2012. The 112th Congress passed it in February 2012. Title I extends the payroll tax reduction. Title II keeps jobless benefits going and seeks to improve the program. Its head note in the table of contents calls the act a set of spurs for job creation.

Subtitle A of Title II reforms jobless pay to promote work. Its sections set steady job search rules and give states more room to help workers find jobs. They also tighten recovery of overpayments and set shared data formats. One section covers drug testing of applicants.
plaw-112-97-2012: Tsunami and flood protection for the Quileute Indian Tribe comes from Public Law 112-97 of the 112th Congress, passed in 2012. The tool is a boundary shift at Olympic National Park in Washington. A map from June 2010, numbered 149/80,059, shows the new lines. Findings place the Quileute Reservation on the west coast of the Olympic Peninsula. The Pacific Ocean borders it on the west, and the park on the other three sides. Most of the village of La Push sits in the coastal zone, the findings begin.
plaw-112-98-2012: Public Law 112-98, the Federal Restricted Buildings and Grounds Improvement Act of 2011, rewrites one crime in title 18. The 112th Congress passed it in 2012 to correct and simplify section 1752. That section covers restricted buildings and grounds. The new text bars a person from knowingly entering or staying in such a place with no lawful right. It also bars wild or disruptive conduct done to impede government work. Blocking entry or exit with that same intent is barred as the sample breaks off.
plaw-112-99-2012: A trade duty tool reaches nonmarket economy countries under Public Law 112-99 of the 112th Congress, passed in 2012. It applies the countervailing duty rules of the Tariff Act of 1930 to nonmarket economy countries. Section 701 gains a new part on such cases. Goods from those countries can now face the duties. One bar stays in place. No duty is required when the trade authority cannot find and measure the subsidies the foreign government gave.
plaw-2012: Private Law 112-1, approved on December 28, 2012, is a private law for the relief of Sopuruchi Chukwueke. For the purposes of the Immigration and Nationality Act, he counts as lawfully admitted to, and as having remained in, the United States. He may seek a change of status to lawful permanent resident if he files, with the proper fees, within two years. One immigrant visa number for his home country is then reduced.
plos-pbio-0020212:
Niels C. Rattenborg, Bruce H. Mandt, William H. Obermeyer, and their team studied sleep in migrating sparrows for PLOS Biology in 2004. White-crowned sparrows fly long distances at night during migration. In cages, they enter a restless state at night in migration season and sleep far less, yet stay alert.

Wild birds cannot afford to be drowsy on long flights, and this species seems to cut sleep without the usual cost. The birds remained able to learn and perform during the day. How they do it is still an open puzzle. The work points to a natural model of sleeplessness without harm, a state sleep science would love to understand.
plos-pbio-0020312:
Paul D. N. Hebert, Mark Y. Stoeckle, Tyler S. Zemlak, and Charles M. Francis tested a DNA identification method for birds in PLOS Biology in 2004. A short, standard stretch of DNA can act as a barcode: read it, match it to a reference list, and name the species.

The team showed the barcode separates bird species with high accuracy, even close kin. One small tissue sample can thus name a bird without an expert eye. That promise has since grown into global libraries used for wildlife trade checks, food fraud, and biodiversity surveys. This bird paper was one of the early proofs that the scheme works at scale.
plos-pbio-0020412:
Jonathan B. Alberts and Garrett M. Odell built a computer model of a moving bacterium in PLOS Biology in 2004. Listeria, a germ that causes food poisoning, hijacks a host cell's actin to push itself around. It rides a comet tail of actin filaments, hopping in small jumps the authors call nano-saltation.

Their in silico model rebuilds that motion from the known parts and reproduces the jerky hops seen under microscopes. A model that matches real motion can be pushed further than any single experiment. It tests which parts matter most and predicts what changes would do. Listeria's trick is also a clean window on how all cells use actin to move and change shape.
plos-pone-0000012:
Don Klinkenberg, Christophe Fraser, and Hans Heesterbeek asked in 2006 how well contact tracing really works when a new epidemic breaks out. Contact tracing means finding the people an infected person has exposed, then isolating or treating them before they spread the disease further. It is slow, costly work.

Using models of emerging infections, the team tested when tracing can hold an outbreak down and when it falls behind. Speed, the share of contacts found, and how fast the disease spreads all change the answer. Their results help health officials judge whether tracing is worth its heavy cost in the first weeks of an epidemic, the moment when control is still possible.
plos-pone-0000112:
Bryant F. McAllister and Amy L. Evans published this genetics study in PLOS ONE in 2006. It looks at Drosophila americana, a North American fruit fly, and asks why some stretches of its DNA carry more variation than expected. The focus is on genes linked to the Y chromosome only part of the time.

Genes on a Y chromosome usually show little variety, because the Y rarely swaps DNA with a partner chromosome. The authors measure diversity in this fly to see what changes when that linkage is only temporary. The work bears on a basic question in evolution: how the layout of chromosomes shapes the genetic variety a species holds.
plos-pone-0000212:
Clément Nizak, Robert J. Fitzhenry, and Richard H. Kessin published this amoeba study in PLOS ONE in 2007. Dictyostelium caveatum is a social amoeba, a microbe that lives in soil and feeds on other microbes. The authors report that it exploits other social amoebae, taking advantage of its relatives rather than only hunting bacteria.

Social amoebae gather and build fruiting bodies together, which creates room for cheating. A species that exploits its cousins shows how far such exploitation can go in microbial societies. The work feeds the wider study of cooperation and conflict among microbes, a model for social evolution at its simplest.
plos-pone-0000312:
Angus M. Tester, Jennifer H. Cox, Andrea R. Connor, and colleagues published this immunology paper in PLOS ONE in 2007. LPS is a bacterial molecule that triggers strong immune reactions, and neutrophils are the first-responder white blood cells. The authors show that responses to LPS, and neutrophil movement toward infection sites in living animals, require MMP-8. MMP-8 is an enzyme from the neutrophils themselves.

An enzyme best known for cutting tissue proteins turns out to be needed for the cells to arrive and respond at all. The paper pins that requirement down in vivo. The result matters for understanding inflammation, where MMP enzymes are often drug targets.
plos-pone-0000412:
Martin Wasser and William Chia studied a fly protein that lives outside the chromosomes, reporting in PLOS ONE in 2007. The protein, called EAST, is extrachromosomal, meaning it is found in the nucleus away from the DNA strands themselves. In the fruit fly Drosophila, it can associate with the giant polytene chromosomes of larval glands.

Beyond sitting on chromosomes, EAST can regulate gene expression, changing which genes are turned on. Proteins that organize the nucleus may control genes by shaping the space they sit in. This work adds to the picture of the nucleus as a structured place, not a bag of loose DNA.
plos-pone-0000512:
Isaac Amela, Juan Cedano, and Enrique Querol tested a reassuring idea about immunity with computation, in a 2007 PLOS ONE paper. When the body makes antibodies against a pathogen, one worry is cross-reaction. The antibody might also attack the host's own proteins. That can happen if the two share epitopes, the small patches antibodies recognize. Their bioinformatics approach compared pathogen proteins that elicit antibodies with host proteins.

The title states their conclusion: such pathogen proteins do not share epitopes with host proteins. If true broadly, the immune system's targeting is cleaner than feared, and vaccine design faces one less hazard. Computational claims of this kind invite experimental spot-checks, which the paper's clear statement makes easy to design.
plos-pone-0000612:
Caroline Fasano, François Tercé, Jean-Pierre Niel and their co-authors reported in PLOS ONE in 2007 on an unusual route for nerve signals. Their study asks whether neurons can pass on excitation without action potentials, the classic electrical spikes. The proposed route rests on ceramide, a fatty molecule made by the cell.

Working with an in vitro model, meaning a lab setup outside a living body, the team tracked how excitation moved along neurons. Action potentials normally lead, after synaptic transmission, to other neurons switching on and networks working as a whole. A ceramide-based path would add a second way for that spread to happen. Readers get a challenge to the standard picture of how nerve cells talk.
plos-pone-0000712:
Srinivasan Ramachandran, Lai-Hua Xie, Scott A. John and co-authors found a new role for a channel protein in cell injury, in PLOS ONE in 2007.
